name: Shenzhen Streets for People with Disabilities: Six Pairwise Questions
description:
Method replication: participants say whether they have a physical, visual, hearing or age-related impairment, then answer six pairwise questions about Shenzhen street scenes from the perspective of their own condition (environmental clarity, barrier-free safety, inclusive vitality, social disconnection, resource accessibility, psychological distress), 8 pairs each, with a "Difficult to judge" option; the images are not the paper's stimuli (87 re-fetched Baidu street views across Futian, Luohu and Nanshan, 2019–2025).

Original study: Lin, Zhang, Qiu & Huang (2026), ISPRS International Journal of Geo-Information 15(6), 274. Baidu street views were collected in four orientations at 201,860 points in Shenzhen. Volunteers from different disability groups compared pairs of street scenes on six dimensions grounded in Attention Restoration Theory, using the comparison instructions in the paper's Table 4; TrueSkill turned the choices into scores used to train a city-wide perception model, combined with segmentation of accessibility elements, social-media sentiment and XGBoost-SHAP analysis of urban restorativeness for people with disabilities.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Baidu street views instead of the authors' images, which are not released; (2) a fixed 8 random pairs per question instead of the authors' comparison set; (3) the screening question on disability type, the demographic questions and the "Difficult to judge" option are added, since the paper does not report its volunteer form; (4) the question wording is the paper's Table 4 instructions; the prediction model and the other analyses are not part of the survey.
author: Lin, Zhang, Qiu & Huang

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: disability
elements.title: Do you have any of the following? (choose all that apply)

choices.text: Physical disability (for example, I use a wheelchair, crutches or a walking aid)
Age-related difficulty walking, seeing or hearing

elements.name: environmental_clarity
elements.title: Which street scene feels easier to navigate and visually clearer for someone with your condition?

elements.name: barrier_free_safety
elements.title: In which street scene do you feel safer moving around, with fewer physical barriers or risks?

elements.name: inclusive_vitality
elements.title: Which street scene gives you a stronger sense that you could be part of the activity, rather than excluded from it?

elements.name: social_disconnection
elements.title: Which street scene makes you feel more isolated, detached, or unwelcome?

elements.name: resource_accessibility
elements.title: In which street scene do you perceive more equitable access to public resources and amenities?

elements.name: psychological_distress
elements.title: Which street scene evokes more feelings of anxiety, unease, or emotional discomfort?
